key_points: AutoDesign = open-source design agent + the reusable DesignHarness evolved by it; MIT licensed; 229 stars, 6 forks; initial public release 2026-08-14, last push 2026-08-18
Positioned explicitly as a better-than-Claude-Design open source alternative for academic communication artifacts (posters, slide decks, webpages, narrated videos)
One paper -> four artifacts ('Paper All-in-One'): poster.html, deck.html/.pdf, index.html webpage, and a narrated 1080p MP4 with timed SRT/VTT subtitles
DesignHarness is harness-agnostic and model-agnostic: works with Codex, Claude Code, Kimi Code, Pi, OpenCode, DeepSeek Harness and any agentic model

Four-stage pipeline: provenance-aware source ingestion -> iterative editable HTML generation/revision -> dual-critic validation (rule-based validator + VLM critic) -> self-contained finalization; up to 12 refinement attempts

Editable by default (native HTML/text/tables, not a flattened image); local-first and inspectable (events, manifests, candidates, validation feedback stay on your machine); installs via `curl -fsSL https://designanything.ai/install.sh | bash` (Node 22+, ffmpeg)
Primary subject: open-source design agent + 'DesignHarness' from Yaxin Luo et al. (Meituan, MBZUAI, HUST, PKU, Tsinghua, CUHK, SJTU); initial public release 2026-08-14
One paper -> four artifacts: editable academic poster (HTML+PDF), 24-slide talk deck (editable PPTX), research webpage, narrated 1080p video with SRT/VTT captions ('Paper All-in-One')
Method is 'meta-harness optimization': a code agent recursively rewrites the harness around FIXED model weights - rollout -> evaluation -> one-component update proposal -> train/dev acceptance gate
Positioning line: 'better than Claude Design on academic communication artifacts production'; DesignHarness is portable to Codex / Claude Code / Kimi Code / Pi / OpenCode / DeepSeek Harness
Repo metrics (2026-09-30): 229 stars, 10 forks, 0 open issues, 3 releases, 2 contributors, Python, last push 2026-09-05
License file resolves to NOASSERTION (no SPDX-recognized license) - self-described as license-clarity work in progress; check before commercial use

Two install routes: one-command launcher (curl -fsSL https://designanything.ai/install.sh | bash; autodesign start; autodesign doctor) needing only Node 22+ and ffmpeg/ffprobe; or source build (Python 3.10+, uv, Playwright browsers, npm)
Four standalone Agent Skills (autodesign-poster / -ppt / -webpage / -video) install into an existing coding agent without running the AutoDesign server

Design constraints: opaque white primary canvas required in all four Skills (so white-background paper figures stay coherent); a reference poster transfers visual system only - never text, claims, logos, QR codes or links as evidence
Editable-by-default and source-grounded: HTML/native text/tables/named assets stay revision-capable, and claims/figures/tables keep provenance beside the run
Repo is Python + Playwright + Node; the demo page https://designanything.ai/ now states the hosted online demo was RETIRED - local install only
Reframes multimodal design generation as a meta-harness optimization problem: the surrounding system around a FIXED model is the optimization target, not model weights

Two nested loops: an inner artifact loop (Designer + Critic produce an execution trajectory) and an outer harness loop (MetaHarnessOptimizer analyses trajectories, evaluator scores, an optimization record and optional human guidance)

Every outer iteration: rollout -> evaluation -> update proposal -> acceptance; exactly ONE harness component is updated per iteration, gated on train gain + development-set retention to prevent overfitting
Introduces PosterBench (100 papers, 5 disciplines: AI/ML, biomedicine & health, climate & earth, economics & policy, physics & astronomy) and the fixed 10-paper PosterBench-mini
Came from a real recursive self-improvement run: 7 days of evolving traces, 224 subagents, 123+ recursive iterations, 54 accepted harness updates
Authors span Meituan, MBZUAI, HUST, Peking University, Tsinghua, CUHK, SJTU (14 authors, Yaxin Luo & Haobin Jiang co-first)
Paper 'AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design', submitted 13 Aug 2026 (arXiv:2608.13560), CS.CV

Typical commercial 'AI research poster maker' competitor page: paste abstract or upload paper -> structured single-page poster (title banner, Introduction/Methods/Results/Conclusions, real-data figures, reference box) in about two minutes, sized A0 or 36x48 in, exports PowerPoint and PDF
Quantifies the pain AutoDesign attacks: researchers routinely spend 6-12 hours on one conference poster, most of it layout rather than intellectual work
States the poster's dual communication job: readable in a 15-second walk-past, rewarding for the 3-minute reader - which is what PosterBench's Readability/Layout weights (25/20) encode
Claims use by researchers at 750+ universities; OCR plus PubMed/Google Scholar citation lookup; free to start, credit/tier pricing

Product-grade competitor: upload a PDF (max 50 MB), it extracts the IMRaD structure, selects figures and lays out a print-ready poster; style presets (Academic/Doraemon/Totoro/Custom), content-density control, 1K-4K resolution, portrait 3:4 default
Credit-metered (15 credits per poster) with a 'fast mode' that skips RAG indexing
Illustrates the commercial pattern AutoDesign competes with: black-box SaaS, per-poster credits, no editable source and no published benchmark
SciSpace's free 'AI scientific poster generator' agent: upload paper or paste abstract, auto-format sections/visuals/references, export PPT or PDF; ~633 runs in the last 7 days
Shows the low end of the market - template-filling agents with no design-quality benchmark, usually producing output that still needs manual refinement

PosterGen (arXiv:2508.17188) is the closest academic predecessor: a four-agent paper-to-poster pipeline (Parser/Curator -> Layout -> Stylist -> Renderer) mirrored on professional poster-designer workflow

Its framing - prior automated approaches 'neglect core design and aesthetic principles, resulting in posters that require substantial manual refinement' - is the exact problem statement AutoDesign reuses

PosterBot (AAAI-22, Xu & Wan) is the original automatic-poster-generation system: select important sections -> generate panels -> integrate the full poster; framed as a special case of document summarization
Establishes the three-generation research lineage AutoDesign cites: PosterBot (2022) -> Paper2Poster/PosterGen/Any2Poster (2025) -> AutoDesign + PosterBench (2026)
Paper2Poster (44.61) and Any2Poster (49.09) remain the weakest baselines on PosterBench, showing how much design quality, not just content extraction, separates the newer systems

angles: The harness, not the model, is the product: AutoDesign keeps model weights frozen and optimizes the system around them — the +5 to +19.6 point gains across seven configurations are the strongest published evidence that scaffolding is the real lever, and the article should lead with that inversion rather than the leaderboard

It beat a closed-source commercial system with an MIT-licensed repo: 78.32 vs Claude Design's 70.87. Open-source-on-academic-artifacts beating a paid product is the headline framing, but the honest caveat is scope — AutoDesign is validated on posters, not general product design

The system evolved itself: DesignHarness was not hand-written; it was recursively optimized over 7 days with 224 subagents, 123+ iterations and 54 accepted updates, each gated on train gain plus development-set retention. Self-improvement as an engineering process, not a marketing claim

PosterBench is the benchmark AND the conflict of interest: the authors introduced the benchmark they lead. Mitigations worth reporting — frozen protocol separate from the optimization-time evaluator, a fixed 10-paper subset, a mandated judge model, and a documented train/development split

The benchmark only weakly predicts human taste (r = 0.34): a score gap has to reach 20 points before reviewers agree with the benchmark about 74% of the time. Anyone quoting '78.32' should quote this number next to it

Real cost economics for a real workflow: under $3 and under 40 minutes for one conference poster, with a Pareto frontier running from $0.27 (LongCat 2.0, 55.13) to $10.02 (GPT-5.5, 81.46) — a genuinely useful decision table for a lab choosing a model route

One paper in, four artifacts out: poster, slide deck, webpage and narrated captioned video from a single source. PosterBench formally validates only the poster, so the other three are demonstrated pilots rather than measured claims — state that boundary plainly

Editable HTML over flattened images is the practical differentiator: native text, tables and named assets survive for revision, versus the image-style output that competitors produce and researchers must rebuild by hand before printing

Positioning against the academic-tool crowd, not just design tools: Paper2Poster (NeurIPS 2025, 44.61) and P2P (ICLR 2026) are the real research lineage, while Canva/BioRender/ChatSlide/Veeso occupy the commercial poster-generator lane with different constraints (A0/A1 sizing, 300 DPI export, print bleed)

The category's unmet gap is print production, not generation: roundups show almost no tool states a DPI figure and one explicitly disclaims print resolution, colour matching and bleed. AutoDesign's HTML-first pipeline inherits the same last-mile problem

The Korean-language README (README.ko.md) plus zh-CN and English docs make this one of the few agentic design projects shipping localised docs from day one — a real signal for non-English research communities

Harness beats model: holding the model fixed and only improving the surrounding harness moves PosterBench scores +5.01 to +19.56 points (average +12.4%) - the same model-plus-better-harness story readers can apply to their own agent stacks, and the sharpest reframe of the 'which model is best' debate

Conflict-of-interest caveat to state plainly: the team that built the harness also built the benchmark and ran the evaluation, using their own judge protocol (gemini-3.5-flash) - treat 78.32 vs Claude Design 70.87 as author-reported, not third-party verified

Benchmark-reality check worth citing: PosterBench only correlates r = 0.34 with human preference, and agreement is 51.9% on close scores - a reminder that a 7-point benchmark lead is not automatically a visible quality lead

Local-first pivot as a buying decision: the hosted demo is retired, so the entire value proposition is now 'runs on your machine with your own API keys' - great for confidential or unpublished papers, but it puts install and maintenance cost on the user (Node 22+, ffmpeg, or Python/uv/Playwright for source builds)

License risk: the repo reports NOASSERTION with no SPDX-recognized license. Anyone planning commercial or client work should confirm terms before adopting, unlike OpenDesign (Apache-2.0) and Open CoDesign (MIT)

Maturity reality check: 229 stars, 10 forks, 2 contributors, 3 releases, 0 open issues in a repo whose last push was 2026-09-05 - a research artifact, not a maintained product; contrast with OpenDesign's 98.9k stars / 11.5k forks and Open CoDesign's 7.9k

Three-way positioning for buyers: AutoDesign = academic-artifact specialist with a published poster benchmark; OpenDesign = general collaborative design workspace with 16 coding-agent backends, design systems and a paid cloud plan; Open CoDesign = BYOK local desktop app for UI prototypes and decks. AutoDesign wins academic posters; the others win product design and team workflows

The $3 / 40-minute number versus the 6-12 hours researchers actually spend per poster is the concrete ROI hook - pair it with the Pareto table (LongCat 55.13 at $0.27 vs GPT-5.5 81.46 at $10.02) to show the quality/cost dial

Editable-by-default is the real differentiator against every credit-metered SaaS poster maker (PaperBanana 15 credits/poster, SciSpace, ChatSlide): AutoDesign output is HTML/native text/tables plus rendered poster, so you can actually fix a caption or swap a figure instead of regenerating
Autonomy still loses to a human nudge: 80.88 autonomous plateau vs 88.39 with human guidance on the representative case - use it to argue for a review step, not blind trust

Portable DesignHarness is the deeper story than the product: the same learned harness lifts Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code, OpenCode, ZCode and a half-dozen models, which is what 'meta-harness optimization' means in practice
